title: kate-search: skip a one-hit replace that copies the hit
summary: replace_one inserts nothing when the replacement text equals the hit. A different replacement still inserts one edit. The test goes in the existing bar tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

definitions.definition: pub fn replace_one(&self, buf: &TextBuffer, hit: &Match) -> Result<Transaction, SearchError>

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: bar.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Do not add a second module with the same name. Change only replace_one. Keep the signature. Keep this line: let new = expanded_replacement(self, buf, hit)?; Do not match the Result by hand. Then let old = slice_text(buf.text(), hit.range); One if returns early. if old == new { return Ok(Transaction::default()); }. Then build the Edit and return Transaction::single as the function does now. Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not touch query, find_from, replace_all, hit_count, or expanded_replacement. The existing plain_replacement_keeps_a_dollar test stays green. The test a_same_replacement_inserts_nothing uses the helper sample. A plain bar that finds a and replaces it with a on the buffer aba returns a transaction that is_empty. A plain bar that replaces a with b returns one edit whose new text is b. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines.

regression_tests.name: bar::tests::a_same_replacement_inserts_nothing
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. Replacing a with a inserts one edit. After the change the transaction is empty. Replacing a with b still inserts one edit whose new text is b.
